response.title: what is the best battery backup for home wifi
response.answer:
For keeping your home Wi-Fi running during a power outage, I recommend a small uninterruptible power supply (UPS) rather than a large portable power station.

A UPS automatically switches to battery power when electricity goes out, usually without interrupting your internet connection.

The best choice depends on whether you want 30 minutes, 2 hours, or 8+ hours of backup.

One important detail: You need to power both your modem/ONT and your Wi-Fi router. If you have fiber internet, the optical network terminal (ONT) also needs power. Your ISP's network must remain operational during the outage.

My top recommendations

Best overall

CyberPower LE1000DG

Approximately $130–$140

4.5 hours at 20W

Independently measured by Wirecutter. Automatic voltage regulation, six battery-backed outlets, and a three-year warranty. 
Reviews by Wirecutter

APC BE600M1 Back-UPS 600VA, 120V, 1 USB charging port, 7 NEM…

$94.99 at newegg.com

Best compact, affordable option

Five battery-backed outlets. APC's published runtime is 4.3 hours at 10W, but actual runtime depends heavily on power consumption. 
WiFi Weekly

Shop

CyberPower CP1350AVRLCD3

Approximately $196

Best for longer backup

A larger UPS with approximately 4.5 hours of tested runtime for a modem and router, according to Wirecutter's testing summary.

My recommendation: For a typical home router and modem, I'd choose the CyberPower LE1000DG. If you want to stay online overnight, consider a larger lithium battery system instead.

One question: How long do you want your Wi-Fi to stay running during a power outage — 1–2 hours, 4–6 hours, or 8–12+ hours? That will make a big difference in which battery is best.
